To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the action potential modulates Cx40 junctional conductance by voltage-dependent gating and that the kinetics of junctional conductances correlate with the genesis and propagation characteristics of cardiac action potentials.

Cx40 junctional conductance is modulated by the transjunctional voltage, and that this modulation can account for the conduction delay and block that occurs during the plateau phase of the action potential.

the transjunctional voltage (Vj) of an action potential can cause rapid inactivation of Cx40 junctional conductance and that recovery of junctional currents during the action potential is coincident with recovery of the action potential.
